content:
Apple has finally responded to the sharp rise in memory and other component costs, and has not held back. Some products have seen price increases of more than 50%, while the price of some memory and storage upgrades has simply doubled.

These price increases are likely to remain in place for years, or even permanently…

9to5Mac readers have long been skeptical about whether Apple will cut prices, even if the component shortage eases. More than two-thirds of readers said they expect the price increases to be permanent.

Subsequently, analyst reports pointed out that supply chain pricing will not see any improvement before 2028, and even then the situation will be quite limited. As it stands, today's significantly higher-than-before pricing will remain for at least several years, and may never return to previous levels.

If this turns out to be the case, how will you readers respond? Will you grit your teeth and continue to buy Apple products at the same pace? Will you reduce the number or frequency of Apple purchases? Or take other measures, such as choosing cheaper models, buying refurbished units, or waiting for price drops before making a move?

Please take part in our poll and share your thoughts in the comments section. The poll allows multiple selections, in case you plan to change your spending habits in more than one way.
